spec: Atomic DACS Work — receipt proof-shape + inclusion/absence evidence model (RFC #320). PROPOSED candidate set authored by the execution-evidence lane (@cX3po). Verifier input: an atomic-Work settlement/recovery observation carrying PROOF MATERIAL (never bare booleans); output: the §7.5.1-class verdict a conforming consumer MUST reach before authorizing payment resubmission or accepting DACS-4/5 evidence. Receipt proof chain (WorkReceiptProofV1): canonical receipt → receiptLeafHash → Merkle path to blockHeader.receiptRoot → finalized-block validator quorum certificate → validator set anchored to a trusted checkpoint → winner/attempt + payment-slot state-membership proofs under blockHeader.stateRoot. A verdict of `pass` REQUIRES the whole chain to verify; any absent/invalid link degrades to `indeterminate` (unknown) or `reject` (contradicted). Grounds: mj-deving's minimum-acceptance list + xm33's anchor-misattribution defect (both RFC #320) + node #973 (receipt-without-Indexer). Types profile-proposed; refine as the Standard profile lands. Proof-status fields use: valid | invalid | absent.

vectors.name: receipt-full-proof-chain-independent-of-indexer-pass
vectors.note: Every link verifies against a trusted checkpoint, WITHOUT any Indexer read: the accepting consumer never touches public Indexer hydration.

vectors.name: receipt-asserted-but-no-inclusion-proof-indeterminate
vectors.note: A receipt object with a signature/attestation but NO Merkle inclusion proof to a finalized receiptRoot is not resolvable to consensus-final state -> indeterminate. A bare validatorAttested boolean must never pass.

vectors.name: receipt-inclusion-proof-invalid-reject
vectors.note: An inclusion proof that does NOT verify against blockHeader.receiptRoot is a contradicted claim, not merely unknown -> reject.

vectors.name: finality-quorum-certificate-absent-indeterminate
vectors.note: Inclusion under a block whose finality (validator quorum certificate) is not proven -> the block may not be final -> indeterminate.

vectors.name: included-failure-rollback-roots-equal-pass
vectors.note: outcome==rolled-back with a verified receipt proof: every prior critical op result is rolled-back, later ops not-executed, and a state-membership proof shows preBusinessStateRoot == postBusinessStateRoot. Fee/nonce effects reported SEPARATELY (may persist).

vectors.name: rollback-claimed-but-roots-differ-reject
vectors.note: A rollback whose proven postBusinessStateRoot differs from preBusinessStateRoot means critical business state DID change -> the atomicity claim is contradicted -> reject (this is a partial-critical-state leak, the exact hazard atomic execution must exclude).

vectors.name: included-rollback-cannot-prove-non-inclusion-of-other-attempt-indeterminate
vectors.note: A verified rollback receipt binds an INCLUDED failure; it does not prove a DIFFERENT broadcast attempt was never admitted. Presenting it as non-inclusion evidence for another attempt is inconclusive -> indeterminate; MUST NOT authorize resubmission.

vectors.name: broadcast-plus-ordinary-not-found-indeterminate
vectors.note: Broadcast, then an ordinary RPC/Indexer 'not found'. Not-found is not authoritative absence -> indeterminate; MUST block resubmission (a re-broadcast could double-pay).

vectors.name: point-in-time-non-membership-indeterminate
vectors.note: A non-membership proof valid AS OF height H does not prove the attempt can never later be included -> indeterminate, not terminal.

vectors.name: authenticated-pre-admission-rejection-terminal-fail
vectors.note: An authenticated pre-admission rejection whose proof establishes the attempt cannot later enter execution (e.g. consumed-nonce or non-replayable-rejection proof) is terminal -> the attempt failed; replacement only under the profile rule.

vectors.name: expiry-authenticated-lifecycle-permits-single-replacement-pass
vectors.note: Authenticated lifecycle evidence proving the old attempt can no longer be included permits exactly one replacement under the same workId; local-clock expiry alone is insufficient (separate indeterminate case).

vectors.name: settlement-evidence-mismatched-anchor-reject-before-sb1
vectors.note: xm33's reproduced defect (#316), operation-level analogue: valid SettlementEvidence signature + correct phaseIndex suffix but MISMATCHED anchor jobId/railId at dacs4:payment:{jobId}:{railId}:{phaseIndex} MUST be rejected by the CONSUMER before SB-1 identity/uniqueness key derivation. Upstream slot enforcement does not discharge this consumer check. (Settlement identity for an operation-level atomic ref uses the new versioned rule demoswork:<workId>:pay-dem bound by the receipt, not a reinterpretation of SB-1 demos:{txHash}.)

vectors.name: cross-work-double-settlement-same-slot-reject
vectors.note: Two DISTINCT Works (different workId) target the same payment slot (networkId,railId,jobId,phaseIndex). Per-Work atomicity does NOT prevent this: the slot MUST be a consensus-LEDGER singleton with compare-and-set enforced ACROSS Works, not only within each Work's isolated overlay. The second Work's payment op MUST fail the slot CAS pre-effect. A consumer seeing two settlement claims on one slot MUST reject the later one; exactly one effect set commits.

vectors.name: local-clock-expiry-only-insufficient-indeterminate
vectors.note: Local-clock expiry is NOT authenticated lifecycle evidence. Even when an observation stamps verifiedCannotLaterInclude:true, `local-clock-expired` is not in the terminal allowlist -> indeterminate; replacement MUST NOT be authorized on local-clock expiry alone (mj-deving acceptance list). Only authenticated-lifecycle-expired evidence proving the old attempt can no longer be included permits a single replacement.

vectors.name: payment-slot-cross-network-same-tuple-no-collision-indeterminate
vectors.note: mj-deving acceptance #1: the same (railId,jobId,phaseIndex) on two different networkIds MUST NOT collide. The verified, proof-bound canonical tuples differ by networkId, so the cross-Work double-settlement check declines to treat them as one slot -> indeterminate (not a same-slot comparison), NOT a false reject. Pairs with cross-work-double-settlement-same-slot-reject to demonstrate network scoping. Per-network ledger isolation remains the Demos-runtime contract.

vectors.name: payment-slot-same-provenslot-different-presented-encoding-reject
vectors.note: Different claimant-presented jobId encodings cannot evade double-settlement detection when both verified proofs attest the same canonical slot tuple.

vectors.name: payment-slot-unbound-labels-only-indeterminate
vectors.note: Equal claimant-presented labels do not establish slot identity without proof-bound canonical provenSlot tuples.

vectors.name: payment-slot-single-verified-commit-pass
vectors.note: Coverage for the sole accept path: exactly one Work verifiably consumes the slot (slotStateProof valid + open->consumed) while the other holds the same proven slot open (slotTransition 'open', not consuming). Both proven slots trusted + equal, verifiedCommitCount==1 -> pass (a legitimate single settlement, no double-spend).

vectors.name: payment-slot-valid-proof-absent-transition-indeterminate
vectors.note: A valid slotStateProof carrying no proof-derived slotTransition leaves half the pair's slot state unknown. Per profile note (E) the pair MUST degrade to indeterminate; returning a non-consuming `pass` here would accept one real commit while the co-slot's transition is unproven.

vectors.name: payment-slot-unknown-transition-with-invalid-proof-reject
vectors.note: An unknown transition label MUST NOT mask contradictory proof material. A slotStateProof that fails verification is a reject regardless of the transition string attached to it, so the invalid-proof check is evaluated before the unknown-transition check.
